notes: All 11 HVS-named stars are recorded as follow_up rather than candidates_found: the paper revisits a pre-existing set of 11 candidate HVSs selected from Brown et al. (2015) HST targets (T:p1-b7, T:p2-b10). HVS 3 is also HE 0437-5439 (T:p1-b13). HVS 1, HVS 4, HVS 6, HVS 9, HVS 10, and HVS 13 are in the final six-star insufficient-astrometry group, while HVS 3, HVS 5, HVS 7, HVS 8, and HVS 12 are among the five unbound stars (T:p7-b8). HVS 2 is mentioned only as the excluded sdO star (T:p2-b10). B434, B485, B711, and B733 are the four radial-velocity outliers called bound in the final assessment (T:p7-b8), so they are not included. The phrase HVS 1 to HVS 13 (T:p3-b7) is not expanded because HVS 2 is excluded and HVS 11 is not analyzed; Table 2 lists only the 11 HVS entries above (T:p4-b0). No Gaia source identifiers are supplied.

HVS 1: For HVS 1, Table 2 (T:p4-b0) marks the entry as “HVS 1 (H)”, so the tabulated proper motions are HST measurements rather than Gaia DR2. The paper reports model-dependent Galactic rest-frame velocities and bound probabilities for Models I–III; I list each model separately. It does not report a separate unbound probability, equatorial coordinates, parallax, or current Galactocentric radius for HVS 1. The Cartesian coordinates and plane-crossing radius r_p in Tables A.1–A.3 (T:p11-b1, T:p12-b0, T:p13-b0) are not the present-day three-dimensional Galactocentric radius.

HVS 3: Target HVS 3 is HE 0437-5439 (T:p1-b13). The T:p6-b4 transcription renders the Przybilla et al. (2008b) comparison value as "61 9 kpc"; I interpret it as 61 ± 9 kpc in the distance entry. No present-day Galactocentric radius, RA, or Dec is explicitly reported for HVS 3: Tables A.1-A.3 list Cartesian x, y, z and a plane-crossing radius r_p, not the current three-dimensional Galactocentric radius. Only bound probability P_b is tabulated, so no unbound_probability entries are submitted.

HVS 4: HVS 4 is analyzed in Table 2 and Tables A.1-A.3. The paper does not report equatorial coordinates or a Gaia parallax for HVS 4. It lists current Galactocentric Cartesian coordinates but does not tabulate a present-day three-dimensional Galactocentric radius; the tabulated r_p values refer to the Galactic-plane crossing, so they were not used as the current galactocentric radius. HST proper motions for HVS 4 are mentioned, but no numerical HST proper-motion values for HVS 4 are tabulated.

HVS 5: Tables 2 and A.1-A.3 give median values with 1-sigma Monte Carlo confidence limits; asymmetric errors are reported as lower_error/upper_error. The current galactocentric radius r = (x^2+y^2+z^2)^(1/2) is defined in the notes to Table A.1, but only the plane-crossing radius r_p is tabulated, so no current galactocentric radius is reported for HVS 5. HST proper motions exist for HVS 5 (two epochs of ACS positions; Brown et al. 2015), but no numerical HST values for this star are tabulated in the paper, so only Gaia DR2 proper motions are recorded. Unbound probability is not explicitly reported (only P_b, the bound probability).

HVS 6: HVS 6 has no reported right ascension, declination, or parallax in the supplied material. The Appendix tables list only a plane-crossing galactocentric radius r_p, not the present-day galactocentric radius, so galactocentric_radius is omitted. Only P_b is reported; no unbound probability is tabulated. The v_Grf value is the same in Models I–III but is recorded separately for each model. Relevant locations: T:p4-b0, I:p11-b1, I:p12-b0, and I:p13-b0.

HVS 7: No equatorial coordinates or annual parallax for HVS 7 are reported in the supplied material. Table A.1 defines a Galactocentric radius r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^(1/2) but does not tabulate the current r; only the present-day Cartesian x, y, z and plane-crossing r_p are given, so no galactocentric_radius is extracted (T:p11-b1). The paper reports bound probabilities P_b only; unbound probabilities are not separately reported and are not derived here.

HVS 8: No equatorial coordinates or parallax for HVS 8 are reported in the supplied material. The only galactocentric radius listed for HVS 8 is the plane-crossing value r_p = 19.8 kpc in Table A.1 (T:p11-b1); because the rules require the present-day state for positions, this past plane-crossing radius is not included as galactocentric_radius. The bound probability is model dependent: 16% for Model I, 0% for Model II, and 100% for Model III.

HVS 9: HVS 9 has no HST-suffix (H) in Table 2, i.e. its proper motions are from Gaia DR2 (the paper states Gaia DR2 and HST proper motions are of similar quality for HVS 4, HVS 6, and HVS 9). T:p4-b0 and I:p4-b0 give the Model I results also quoted in the main text; T:p11-b1 (Table A.1, Model I), T:p12-b0 (Table A.2, Model II) and T:p13-b0 (Table A.3, Model III) list the per-model Galactic rest-frame velocities and bound probabilities. No equatorial coordinates (ra, dec), parallax, or explicit galactocentric radius is reported for HVS 9; the tables give only its Cartesian Galactocentric position (x, y, z). Unbound probabilities are not reported directly (P_b = 0% in Models I and II implies the star is treated as unbound there). Errors for the Model I/II/III values are asymmetric 1-sigma Monte Carlo confidence limits; for the distance and radial velocity the asymmetric errors are taken as reported in Table 2.

HVS 10: HVS 10 is marked (H) in Table 2 (T:p4-b0 / I:p4-b0), so its tabulated proper motions are HST values rather than Gaia DR2 values. The paper does not report equatorial coordinates, a parallax, a current Galactocentric radius, or an unbound probability for HVS 10. The bound probability is model-dependent: 29% in Model I, 0% in Model II, and 100% in Model III.

HVS 12: HVS 12 is listed as HVS 12 (H) in Table 2 and Tables A.1–A.3; the (H) suffix means its proper motions are from HST rather than Gaia DR2, because Gaia DR2 proper motions are not superior for this star (T:p2-b11; T:p4-b0). The paper does not report RA, Dec, parallax, or a current three-dimensional galactocentric radius for HVS 12; Table A.1 gives x, y, z but no current r, so no galactocentric radius was extracted. Bound probabilities P_b are reported; unbound probabilities are not explicitly tabulated.

HVS 13: For HVS 13, the paper does not report equatorial coordinates, parallax, or an explicit present-day three-dimensional Galactocentric radius. Tables A.1-A.3 list Cartesian positions and the plane-crossing radius r_p, but r_p is not the present-day galactocentric radius, so it was not used for galactocentric_radius. The listed proper motions are the HST values adopted for HVS 13 (suffix H); Gaia DR2 values are not given numerically for this star. Bound probabilities are reported separately for the three Milky Way models and all are retained. All uncertainties are the paper's 1σ values.
